approach: Add one gate helper, attribution::after_cutover(git, commit) -> Result<Option<String>>, returning C0 only when the commit's athena.toml names a cutover_job, cutover_state is Shown, and C0 is the commit or its ancestor. Use it to (1) strip Athena-* trailer lines in the commit writers (Committer::build_commit_in in commits.rs, commit_with_staged in manage.rs) when the parent is at or after C0; (2) skip only invariant::check in the gate for changes whose first parent is at or after C0, as check_history already does; (3) keep every trailer reader on its grep path for commits up to C0 and add a C0..head path/record fallback, with the squash-text check relaxed only once C0 is shown. Attribution after C0 comes from landing records written by Athena's own land_pr path: classify_commit (land.rs) classifies every commit of a PR by content (JobLanding, DeclaredIntervention via records/interventions/..., RecordsOnly), and the landing record names the PR's commits. So a landing, an intervention and a records-only commit each get attributed by landing their PR through land_pr with a fake host; no hand-written records.

decisions.choice: Strip Athena- trailers once, in the commit-writing functions, keyed on the parent's cutover state.
decisions.reason: Plumbing commits go through Committer::build_commit_in and staged interventions through commit_with_staged; one filter covers about 40 message(..., trailers) call sites, and 'before C0 shows, trailers still written' is one check.

rejected.why: About 40 edits; easy to miss one.
message() is pure with no git or cutover knowledge; pre-C0 callers need trailers.

decisions.choice: Decide 'after C0' from the parent commit's own athena.toml: cutover_job set, cutover_state Shown, C0 equals or is an ancestor of the parent.
decisions.reason: Same condition check_history uses; C0 keeps trailers, the next commit is the first without. Unset, no landing record or Pending gives None, so criterion 4 holds.

rejected.option: Read the checkout's athena.toml or a global flag
rejected.why: The checkout can differ from the commit's config.

decisions.choice: Gate skips only invariant::check for changes whose first parent is at or after C0; secrets, content and jobs checks stay. Recorded in docs/decisions.md under D111 as a decision, not left open.
decisions.reason: history.rs:161 runs invariant::check only for commits up to C0, so the commit-time skip matches the history check; without trailers names_existing_work would refuse Athena's own records-only commits. Attribution against records judges them afterwards. A gate test shows that after C0 a commit with a secret, a content violation and a jobs violation is still refused, and that a trailer-less records-only commit passes after C0 and is refused before.

rejected.why: Athena's own trailer-less commits would be refused.

rejected.option: Skip the whole gate after C0
rejected.why: Drops secrets, content and jobs safeguards for no reason.

decisions.choice: Readers keep the trailer path and add a C0..head fallback; the squash-text check relaxes only when C0 is shown (Git::squash_text stays strict, new squash_text_with takes a flag).
decisions.reason: Deleting trailer reading is out of scope and criterion 3 needs unchanged results up to C0; grep results come first, so a union cannot change them.

rejected.option: Switch all readers to records lookup
rejected.why: Changes pre-C0 behaviour and drops trailer reading.

decisions.choice: Show attribution with Athena's own entry points: the scratch test lives in the gh.rs test module (it has the fake host World and GitLandingRecords), makes three pull requests (job landing, declared intervention, records-only), lands each with land_pr after a shown cutover, then runs check_history and check_attribution_with_legacy (the functions behind athena check --history/--attribution). The test writes no landing records by hand.
decisions.reason: Tracing showed landing records are written only by land_pr (GitLandingRecords::landing) and reconcile; there is no production writer for DeclaredIntervention records (only reconcile tests write them) and none is needed, because classify_commit attributes intervention and records-only commits through the PR's landing record. Cutover records themselves (import, legacy-exempt) come from the cutover hook GitLandingRecords::cutover that land_pr already calls, so the test lands the cutover job through land_pr too.

rejected.option: Write landing records by hand in lifecycle.rs
rejected.why: Would not show Athena attributes the commits (critic finding 4).

decisions.choice: Drop run.rs, main.rs and land.rs from the plan; land.rs classification is content-only (messages never read) and needs no change. No run.rs or main.rs change is planned.
decisions.reason: Tracing land.rs showed classification ignores messages. I did not find a trailer dependency in run.rs or main.rs; if the producer finds one it reports it as an open item rather than silently widening.

rejected.why: Conditional deliverables are hard to check.

demonstrations.method: In-crate scratch repository test (gh.rs World with fake host): land the cutover job through land_pr so records show C0; then land three PRs through land_pr (a job landing, an intervention with records/interventions/<month>/<id>.json, a records-only commit). Read each commit's message.
demonstrations.observes: None of the three commit messages has a line starting 'Athena-'; the records branch holds landing records, written by land_pr, whose commits list names each of the three commits with kinds JobLanding, DeclaredIntervention and RecordsOnly.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the strip in build_commit_in/commit_with_staged the messages keep Athena-Job/Intervention lines and the assertion fails; without the gate skip the trailer-less records-only commit is refused; without land_pr's landing records the kinds assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Same test, after the three landings, runs athena_gate check_history and check_attribution_with_legacy on HEAD, the functions behind athena check --history and --attribution.
demonstrations.observes: Both reports have no violations and no unattributed commits for the post-C0 commits.
demonstrations.fails_without: If post-C0 commits were still judged by trailers, or the landing records did not attribute them, the reports list violations and the empty-report assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Named tests: status.rs reader_after_c0_trace_uses_trailers_up_to_c0, auditor.rs reader_after_c0_changed_files_use_trailers_up_to_c0 (both build trailer-bearing commits up to C0 and a post-C0 job, and compare pre-C0 results with the no-cutover results), and athena-git squash_text_stays_strict (zero or two Athena-Job trailers still refused). Also gh.rs reader_after_c0_landed_commit_uses_trailer_up_to_c0.
